title: How Founders Can Extend Runway Before Their Next Raise
summary: How Founders Can Extend Runway Before Their Next Raise
body_markdown:
How startups can extend runway before their next raise


For startup founders, runway is one of the most important numbers to understand.


It tells you how much time your company has to reach the next milestone before you need additional funding.


But extending runway isn’t just about cutting costs or putting growth on pause. The best startups know how to make their cash work harder while continuing to invest in the things that matter most.


At Fondo, we work with startups at every stage of growth, and one thing we see often is that founders don’t always have full visibility into where their money is going until they’re already thinking about the next raise.


The earlier you understand your burn, expenses, and financial trends, the more options you have.


Here are some practical ways founders can extend runway without slowing momentum.


## 1. Know your true burn rate


Your monthly spend is not the same thing as your burn rate.


Burn rate measures how quickly your company is using cash over time. Understanding your[true burn](https://fondo.com/blog/cash-burn-rate) helps you answer important questions:


- How many months of runway do we have?
- Which expenses are driving the most spend?
- Are we investing in areas that move the business forward?
- What changes would meaningfully extend our runway?


A lot of startups look at their bank balance and estimate runway from there. But without accurate financials, that number can be misleading.


For example, upcoming annual payments, outstanding invoices, payroll changes, or planned hires can all impact how long your cash actually lasts.


## 2. Review your biggest expenses


Not every expense deserves the same level of scrutiny.


Start by looking at your largest spending categories:


- Payroll
- Contractors
- Software subscriptions
- Marketing spend
- Cloud infrastructure
- Vendor costs


The goal isn’t to cut everything.


Early-stage startups need to spend money to grow. The question is whether each expense is helping you reach your next milestone.


A $200/month tool that saves your team hours every week may be worth keeping. A collection of unused subscriptions quietly charging your card every month may not be.


## 3. Build a hiring plan around milestones


Hiring is often the biggest decision impacting runway.


Growing your team can help you move faster, but every new hire changes[your financial picture](https://fondo.com/blog/the-founders-hiring-payroll-guide) .


Before adding headcount, consider:


- What milestone will this hire help you reach?
- Is this role essential right now?
- Could a contractor help you get there first?
- How does this impact your runway?


Strong hiring decisions are about timing, not just talent.


## 4. Make sure you’re taking advantage of available tax savings


Many startups focus on reducing expenses but overlook opportunities to recover cash.


The R&D tax credit is one example.


If your team is building software, developing new technology, or solving technical challenges, your startup may qualify for valuable tax credits.


For eligible startups, the R&D tax credit can help offset development costs and preserve cash that can be reinvested into growth.


It’s one reason we encourage founders to think about tax strategy throughout the year, not just during tax season.


## 5. Keep your financial reporting up to date


Good financial decisions require good financial information.


Founders should be able to quickly answer:


- How much cash do we have?
- What is our monthly burn?
- What is our runway?
- Are expenses increasing or decreasing?
- How are we tracking against our plan?


Clean books and reliable reporting aren’t just for[tax compliance](https://fondo.com/blog/sales-tax-complaince-outsourcing-for-business-startups) . They help you make faster decisions.


They also become increasingly important as you prepare for fundraising, investor updates, and board conversations.


## 6. Plan your next raise before you need it


One of the biggest mistakes startups make is starting fundraising when runway is already running low.


Investors want to see momentum, not urgency.


Give yourself enough time to raise by understanding:


- Your current runway
- Your fundraising timeline
- The milestones you want to hit before raising
- The metrics investors will care about


The more financial clarity you have, the stronger position you’re in when it’s time to raise.


Extend your runway with better financial visibility


Extending runway isn’t about spending as little as possible.


It’s about knowing where your money is going and making intentional decisions about where to invest.


With accurate financials, proactive tax planning, and a clear understanding of your burn, you can give your startup more time to build, grow, and reach its next milestone.
